context.name: Context
context.label: Encore in the world
context.blurb: Who touches the ticketing platform, and what it depends on to do its job.

nodes.name: Ticket buyer
nodes.desc: Finds a show, picks seats, pays. Expects the seat they picked to still be there 90 seconds later.

nodes.name: Promoter
nodes.desc: Publishes shows, sets price bands and on-sale times, watches sales in real time.

nodes.name: Encore Ticketing
nodes.desc: Sells seats for live events. Holds inventory, takes money, issues tickets and lets staff scan them at the door.

nodes.name: Gate scanner app
nodes.desc: Handheld scanners at the venue. Works without signal and reconciles scans when it reconnects.

nodes.name: Stripe
nodes.desc: Card authorisation and capture. Encore never stores a card number.

nodes.name: Twilio + SendGrid
nodes.desc: Delivers tickets, receipts, door-time reminders and release notices.

nodes.name: NetSuite
nodes.desc: Receives a nightly settlement file: gross sales, fees, refunds, per promoter.

containers.name: Containers
containers.label: Inside Encore Ticketing
containers.blurb: The deployable pieces and the stores they own. Dashed lines are asynchronous — nobody is waiting on the other end.

nodes.name: Box office web
nodes.desc: Public storefront and the promoter console. Server-renders the seat map, then talks JSON for everything after that.

nodes.name: Gate scanner app
nodes.desc: Queues scans locally when the venue wifi drops and replays them in order once it is back.

nodes.name: API gateway
nodes.desc: One front door. Verifies the session, attaches tenant and trace id, sheds load per promoter during an on-sale rush.

nodes.name: Catalog service
nodes.desc: Shows, venues, seat maps, price bands. Read-heavy and aggressively cached — this is what survives the on-sale spike.

nodes.name: Seat inventory
nodes.desc: The only thing allowed to say a seat is taken. Places short-lived holds, promotes them to allocations, releases them when they lapse.

nodes.name: Order service
nodes.desc: Owns the checkout saga: confirm the hold, price it, charge it, record it, announce it. Compensates in reverse if any step fails.

nodes.name: Gate API
nodes.desc: Validates a scanned barcode against the order state and rejects the second scan of the same ticket.

nodes.name: Catalog store
nodes.desc: Show and seat-map definitions. Written rarely, read constantly.

nodes.name: Hold store
nodes.desc: One key per held seat with an eight-minute expiry. The expiry is the business rule — nothing needs to remember to clean up.

nodes.name: Order store
nodes.desc: Orders, line items, idempotency keys and an outbox so an order and its event are committed together.

nodes.name: Payment adapter
nodes.desc: Wraps Stripe. Translates their objects into ours and turns late webhooks into events the rest of us understand.

nodes.name: Stripe
nodes.desc: External card processor.

nodes.name: Event bus
nodes.desc: Everything that already happened gets announced here: order.paid, hold.expired, ticket.issued, ticket.scanned.

nodes.name: Ticket issuer
nodes.desc: Mints the barcode, renders the PDF and the wallet pass, then announces ticket.issued.

nodes.name: Notifier
nodes.desc: Turns events into messages people actually receive, with per-recipient deduplication.

nodes.name: Twilio + SendGrid
nodes.desc: External delivery.

orders.components.name: Order service
orders.components.label: Inside the order service
orders.components.blurb: A saga in seven moves. Anything to the right of the dividing line lives outside this container.

nodes.name: OrderController
nodes.desc: Validates the request body, pulls the idempotency key off the header, hands off. Contains no business rules on purpose.

nodes.name: IdempotencyGuard
nodes.desc: A retried checkout must not charge twice. First writer wins; everyone else gets the stored response.

nodes.name: CheckoutSaga
nodes.desc: The one place that knows the order of operations, and the one place that knows how to undo them.

nodes.name: PricingEngine
nodes.desc: Price band, fees, promoter rebate, tax. No I/O, so it is the easiest thing here to test.

nodes.name: InventoryClient
nodes.desc: Confirms the hold. On timeout it assumes failure and lets the saga compensate.

nodes.name: PaymentClient
nodes.desc: Charges once. Retries are deliberately disabled — reconciliation is the payment adapter's job.

nodes.name: OrderRepository
nodes.desc: Writes the order and its outgoing event in the same transaction. No event, no order.

nodes.name: OutboxPublisher
nodes.desc: Drains the outbox to Kafka. Consumers must tolerate a duplicate, and they do.

nodes.name: Seat inventory
nodes.desc: Another container.

nodes.name: Payment adapter
nodes.desc: Another container.

nodes.name: Order store
nodes.desc: This container owns it.

nodes.name: Event bus
nodes.desc: Shared bus.

inventory.components.name: Seat inventory
inventory.components.label: Inside seat inventory
inventory.components.blurb: Small on purpose. The correctness of the whole platform rests on these four parts.

nodes.name: HoldController
nodes.desc: Takes a seat list and a session, returns a hold id and the second it expires.

nodes.name: SeatAllocator
nodes.desc: Claims every requested seat or none of them, in one round trip, so two buyers cannot split a pair.

nodes.name: ExpiryReaper
nodes.desc: Listens for expired hold keys and announces the seats as free again. No polling loop.

nodes.name: HoldStore
nodes.desc: The only code allowed to speak to Redis. Keeps the key format in exactly one file.

nodes.name: Hold store
nodes.desc: Seat keys with a TTL.

nodes.name: Event bus
nodes.desc: Shared bus.

cues.title: Checkout submitted
cues.note: The browser posts the hold id and a Stripe payment token. Idempotency-Key is set from the cart, so a double-click is harmless.

cues.title: Routed
cues.note: Gateway checks the session, stamps tenant and trace-id, forwards to the order service.

cues.title: Confirm the hold
cues.note: The saga asks inventory to promote the hold to an allocation. 400ms budget — a timeout is treated as a no.

cues.title: Seats locked down
cues.note: The hold key loses its TTL and becomes permanent. From here the seats belong to this order.

cues.title: Charge
cues.note: £74.50 for two stalls seats plus fee. Retries are off; one attempt only.

cues.title: Captured
cues.note: PaymentIntent confirmed against the token the browser already collected.

cues.title: Order written
cues.note: Order rows and the order.paid outbox row commit in one transaction. This is the point of no return.

cues.title: Announced
cues.note: The outbox publisher drains the row onto Kafka. At-least-once, so consumers deduplicate.

cues.title: Tickets minted
cues.note: Barcode, PDF and wallet pass generated, then ticket.issued goes back on the bus.

cues.title: Message queued
cues.note: Same event, different consumer. Notifier does not know or care that fulfilment exists.

cues.title: Delivered
cues.note: Email with the pass attached, SMS with the door time. The buyer sees a confirmation about 1.4s after they clicked.

cues.title: TTL runs out
cues.note: Eight minutes with no checkout. Redis expires the seat key on its own — no cleanup job, no cron.

cues.title: Seats released
cues.note: hold.expired is published. The seat map goes green again for everyone watching.

cues.title: Buyer told
cues.note: "Your seats were released." Sent once per session, not once per seat.

cues.title: Claim the key
cues.note: First request to claim this Idempotency-Key proceeds. A replay gets the stored response and stops here.

cues.title: Saga starts
cues.note: The controller is done. Everything after this is orchestration.

cues.title: Price it
cues.note: Band, booking fee, promoter rebate, VAT. Pure functions, no I/O.

cues.title: Confirm the hold
cues.note: Step 1 of 3 that can fail. Compensation: none needed yet.

cues.title: Take the money
cues.note: Step 2. If this fails, the saga releases the hold and returns 402.

cues.title: Persist
cues.note: Step 3. If this fails after a successful charge, the saga refunds and alerts — the only path that pages a human.

cues.title: Hand to the outbox
cues.note: The event is already committed. Publishing is now somebody else's problem, which is the point.

cues.title: Barcode replayed
cues.note: Scans batched on the handheld while the venue wifi was down, sent in scan order.

cues.title: Routed to the gate API
cues.note: Higher rate limit for venue IPs — doors open faster than they buy.

cues.title: Ticket looked up
cues.note: Valid, refunded, or already scanned. Second scan of the same barcode returns 409.

cues.title: Attendance recorded
cues.note: ticket.scanned feeds the promoter's live door count.
